claims.text: Si-containing CrFeCoNiX preferentially forms a continuous, coherent inner SiO2 layer during high-temperature oxidation.
Al-containing CrFeCoNiX preferentially forms a continuous, coherent inner Al2O3 layer during high-temperature oxidation.
The SiO2 or Al2O3 inner layer is chemically inert and slow-growing.
A continuous SiO2 or Al2O3 layer resists cracking and spallation.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX forms a non-uniform, mixed-phase oxide.
The oxide on Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX has greater thermal-expansion mismatch than the protective oxides proposed for the Si- and Al-containing alloys.
The oxide on Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX tends to crack during prolonged exposure above 900 °C.
Changing X among Si, Al, and Mn in otherwise composition-matched, identically processed CrFeCoNiX alloys isolates the effect of X on oxide-scale formation.
The nature and coherency of the initially formed oxide scale mediate long-term protection.
The high oxygen affinity of Si and Al drives their preferential oxidation at high temperature.
SiO2 and Al2O3 scales are dense and have low ionic diffusivity.
SiO2 and Al2O3 scales have lower thermal-expansion mismatch with the underlying alloys than the Mn-derived scale.
Low ionic diffusivity causes the proposed SiO2 and Al2O3 barriers to grow slowly.
Lower thermal-expansion mismatch allows the proposed SiO2 and Al2O3 barriers to maintain integrity.
Mn forms mixed-valence oxides that produce a less coherent and more highly stressed barrier.
A less coherent and more highly stressed Mn-derived barrier is prone to cracking and spallation.
Under identical high-temperature exposure, Si- or Al-containing alloys will have more continuous, coherent, slow-growing scales than the Mn-containing baseline.
The Mn-containing alloy is expected to form a non-protective, cracked oxide scale under the comparison conditions.
The proposed behavior is limited to oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C in single- or multiphase metallic solid-solution states.
Microstructural state and local chemical homogeneity may alter oxide-scale performance.
